references.text: The same law concerning the peace offering that is eaten on the third day: it becomes defiled (פִּגּוּל) and shall not be accepted, and whoever eats it shall bear their guilt.
The immediate context providing background for this rule: the peace offering must be eaten on the day of sacrifice or the following day.
A similar principle that the thank offering must be eaten on the same day and not left until the next morning.
Uses the word פִּגּוּל (defiled meat) as a term describing the abominable practices of idol worshippers.
Ezekiel refuses to eat פִּגּוּל (defiled meat), referencing the Levitical laws of purity.
